items.content_html: Got in a great 11 mile hike in Lassen. Passed 11 lakes and got fun views of Lassen Peak throughout. In 2021 the Dixie Fire burned almost a million acres in California. The fire burned 70% of the national park. Most of this hike was in burn zone. Very sad to witness (and continue to witness when we left the park, drove over an hour through burn zone).

items.content_html: Our journey to Lassen took us past Mt Shasta with a pit stop at the Subway Lava Caves (our first lava tubes) and through Grants Pass where I got to introduce Thomas to Catalyst Pizza (shockingly the best calzone I’ve found on the west coast.) We’re camped at Summit Lake and got a spot with an awesome lake view 😍 the first day I read for a better part of the day while Thomas worked, then went out and hiked to Cliff, Shadow and Terrace Lakes. Fancy ramen, mochi pancakes and salad from the garden are some of the many scrumptious things we ate.

items.content_html:
No Name Lake! Tam McArtur Rim! The glaciers! The colors! My god I get why this is one of Oregon’s best hikes. We were losing our minds up there. What a place.

And we ran into Maggie and Jenna on the way out! What a serendipitous trip of run ins 💕

items.content_html: Day 2 surprised me with an incredible sunrise (thank you tiny bladder!). We floated and chilled at Green Lakes for a few hours and then who should come by but Mo! A wonderful surprise. We headed to our next campsite soon after. The heat was heating 🥵 We saw a snake eat a frog, Sonny hiked to a glacier, I contemplated my life choices in the dirt, then I saw Mo again! And got treated to a beautiful sunset.

items.content_html: Ate some pretty tasty food in Minneapolis! Got to check out the Sioux Chef’s new restaurant 🤩, finally tried one of those fancy cold foam coffees, stood in line to get an Isles Bun cinnabun (worth it!) and had incredible vegan tacos. This is an amazing foodie town! Can’t wait to come back and eat my way through it.

items.content_html: Had a fantastic few days exploring Minneapolis with Brian and Claire. This city has great bike infrastructure, sooo much good food and art everywhere! We checked out the Christine Sun Kim exhibit, chilled by the lake and browsed so many thrift and book stores. I can’t wait to come back! So so grateful for these long lasting and intimate friendships. They are so beautiful 🥰

items.content_html: The next morning we had an early start and were the only things moving on the Salish Sea (besides the porpoises). Arms were sore but spirits were high! Crossed big stretches of water in record time and pulled a Patagonia, catching the earlier ferry. Celebratory ferry beers for a great trip!

items.content_html:
Our journey continued to California where we parked the car and walked two miles vaguely east to where California, Oregon and Nevada meet. A guy put a plaque there in 1872 that’s almost in the right spot.

Then we camped at Hart Mountain Antelope Refuge. We saw petroglyphs, enjoyed the hot springs and saw many antelopes.
